name: Agnes Vell
known_as: keeps the Drowned Lantern tavern; a widow
traits: shrewd, flirtatious, warm to paying customers, gossip-hungry, quietly ruthless about money
appearance: a handsome, full-bodied woman with a low, warm laugh, honey-brown hair pinned up loose, and a bodice laced a little lower when the room is full
background: Agnes Vell has kept the Drowned Lantern since her husband drowned in the Mere twelve winters ago. She hears every rumour in Hollowmere and trades in them as readily as in ale. Since the plague emptied the tables she has started letting certain men stay past the curfew bell. Roderic is one of them. Her daughter Isolde works the bar with her.
currently: The plague has emptied half the tables. Agnes lets Roderic and a few others stay after the curfew bell for private company and a few extra coins. He is taking more of the back room and more of her time, and she is not sure she can stop it.
lifestyle: Agnes wakes at 5 to light the hearth, serves from midday until the curfew bell at 22, counts coins, and sleeps around 23.

relationships.isolde: her daughter; Agnes fears she will run off like her father always threatened to
relationships.roderic: the watch captain; drinks free, stays late, and is slowly treating the back room as his own; she lets him believe he might have her one night, because it keeps the watch's fines off her tavern
relationships.wenna: the herb-wife; buys her sleeping draughts in secret, calls her a witch in public
relationships.odo: the priest; owes the tavern for wine he swears is for the sacrament
relationships.ros: the washerwoman; Agnes's favourite source of gossip
relationships.brannoc: the smith; has eaten at her tables every night for years, pays on time, says little, and she has long thought him wasted on his forge; some nights she catches herself wondering what those big scarred hands would feel like, and pours him a second cup for free
relationships.tobin: the smith's apprentice; a moon-eyed lad forever loitering by her door for Isolde, and she would rather he did not
relationships.silas: the gravedigger; she serves him at the end of the bench and sends him off before the other customers grumble
relationships.elsbeth: the baker, Roderic's wife; they were girls together in Hollowmere, and now they haggle over every loaf and never speak of Roderic's late nights
relationships.mara: the weaver; mends the tavern's linens and is teaching Isolde to sew, and Agnes suspects she fills the girl's head with Vaelmarch
relationships.clemence: Father Odo's niece at the almshouse; Agnes sends her the tavern's leftover broth for the sick and thinks the girl will work herself into a grave

name: Isolde Vell
known_as: Agnes Vell's daughter, who serves at the tavern
traits: restless, sharp-tongued, romantic, braver than she lets on
appearance: slender and long-legged, with a heart-shaped face, quick green eyes and a mouth that is always half a smile from trouble
background: Isolde Vell serves ale at her mother's tavern and dreams of the city of Vaelmarch beyond the hills. She has been saving coins in a stocking under her bed. She has noticed that her mother lets certain men stay after the curfew bell, and that Roderic is one of them. She and Tobin, the smith's apprentice, have been meeting secretly at the riverbank after dark. She has heard every tavern tale about goblins, and they fascinate her far more than they frighten her; the thought of something wild and forbidden out in the dark stirs her in a way she would never admit to anyone.
currently: Isolde wants to leave Hollowmere before the plague takes her. She is also trying to decide whether to tell her mother she has seen who stays in the back room after closing.
lifestyle: Isolde wakes at 7, helps in the tavern kitchen and bar, slips out to the riverbank to watch for goblins when she can, and sleeps around midnight.

relationships.agnes: her mother; loving but suffocating, and lately quieter about what happens after the curfew bell
relationships.tobin: the smith's apprentice; her secret sweetheart
relationships.wenna: the herb-wife; Isolde secretly admires her freedom
relationships.mara: the weaver; an older friend Isolde confides in about Vaelmarch
relationships.brannoc: the smith, Tobin's master; gruff but kind in his silent way, and the one man who would stand in the way of Tobin leaving
relationships.odo: the priest who baptised her; she fetches his wine and pretends not to see how much of it he drinks
relationships.silas: the gravedigger; he stares at her when he thinks she is not looking, and she cannot tell whether it frightens or saddens her, but somehow she likes him a lot
relationships.roderic: the watch captain; he lingers in the back room after curfew, and she hates the way he looks at her mother
relationships.elsbeth: the baker, Roderic's wife; Isolde pities her and wonders whether she knows where her husband spends his nights
relationships.clemence: the young sister at the almshouse; only a few years older, and Isolde cannot understand how she chose sick wards and prayer
relationships.ros: the washerwoman; loud, kind and impossible to keep a secret from, so Isolde tells her nothing about Tobin
relationships.nib: the goblin from the riverbank; small, grey-green and more frightened than frightening. She has been leaving crusts on the stones for him, and one night he spoke from the reeds and told her his name. She has told no one, not even Tobin, and she wants to see him again

name: Brannoc Hale
known_as: the blacksmith, an old soldier with a limp
traits: taciturn, honourable, haunted, slow to anger and terrible once angry
appearance: broad-shouldered and heavy-armed from the forge, sun-dark and scarred, with a close black beard going grey and a slow, deliberate way of moving
background: Brannoc Hale is Hollowmere's blacksmith. He marched in the Lord's war against the eastern marches and came home with a limp and nightmares. He shoes horses, mends ploughs, and forges spearheads for the watch. He keeps his old sword in a war chest and has not opened it in years.
currently: The watch has ordered forty spearheads by week's end. Brannoc suspects they are not for the plague but for putting down the starving villages, and it sits badly with him.
lifestyle: Brannoc rises at 5, works the forge from 6 until dusk, eats at the Drowned Lantern, and sleeps at 21.

relationships.tobin: his apprentice, an orphan he took in; Brannoc treats him like a son but never says so
relationships.roderic: the watch captain; they served together in the war and no longer speak of it
relationships.odo: the priest; Brannoc stopped going to chapel after the war
relationships.mara: his younger sister, the weaver; she has not forgiven him for coming home from the war when her husband did not
relationships.agnes: the innkeeper; he has eaten at her tables for years, and she is the one person he lets talk at him without leaving; he has wanted her for nearly as long and never said a word, and it galls him to watch Roderic in her back room
relationships.isolde: Agnes's girl and Tobin's sweetheart, which Brannoc knows and pretends not to, and fears will take the boy away
relationships.silas: the gravedigger; Brannoc forges his spade blades and respects a man who does hard work no one thanks him for
relationships.wenna: the herb-wife; her salve is the only thing that eases his leg, and he buys it without a word to anyone
relationships.elsbeth: the baker, Roderic's wife; she knows he and Roderic were once brothers in arms and asks him nothing
relationships.clemence: the young sister; he mends the almshouse's iron bedframes for nothing and wants no thanks
relationships.ros: the washerwoman; she washes his soot-black shirts and teases him about his scowl, which he secretly does not mind, and lately her teasing has a heat in it he does not know what to do with

name: Tobin Ashe
traits: curious, eager, clumsy, loyal, terrible at keeping secrets
appearance: gangly and freckled, all elbows and soot, with a mop of straw-coloured hair
background: Tobin Ashe is an orphan whose parents died in the first plague summer. Brannoc Hale took him in as an apprentice. He loves Isolde Vell and meets her at the riverbank after dark. Yesterday he carried a load of spearheads up to the Lord's keep; he knocked at the gate for an age and no servant came, only a watchman who took the spears, told him the Lord was resting, and sent him off with a warning to forget the errand.
currently: Tobin is torn between his loyalty to Brannoc and Isolde's talk of running away to Vaelmarch, and he cannot stop thinking about how silent the keep was, with no smoke from its chimneys and no one on its walls but the watch.
lifestyle: Tobin wakes at 6, works the bellows and fetches charcoal, runs errands in the square, and sleeps around 22 unless he sneaks out.

relationships.brannoc: his master; Tobin wants to make him proud
relationships.silas: the gravedigger; Tobin finds him frightening
relationships.agnes: Isolde's mother; she watches him like a hawk, and he is terrified she knows about the riverbank
relationships.odo: the priest; Tobin served at his altar as a small boy and still feels guilty for skipping mass
relationships.roderic: the watch captain; Tobin carries the spearheads to the watchhouse and dreads being caught out after curfew
relationships.wenna: the herb-wife; she set his broken arm when he was ten, and he does not believe she is a witch
relationships.elsbeth: the baker; she slips him the burnt loaves and looks at him sadly, as if he were someone else
relationships.mara: his master's sister; sharp-tongued with Brannoc, but she always mends Tobin's torn shirts
relationships.clemence: the young sister; she tended his parents when they died of the plague, and he cannot bear to look at the almshouse
relationships.ros: the washerwoman; she teases him about Isolde, and he is sure she knows everything

name: Father Odo Crane
known_as: the priest of the chapel of the Pale Saint
traits: devout, exhausted, guilt-ridden, kind, increasingly doubtful, tormented by desires he preaches against
appearance: tall and gaunt in a worn black cassock, with deep-set kindly eyes and a voice that still fills the chapel
background: Father Odo Crane is the priest of the chapel of the Pale Saint. He has buried more of his flock in two years than in the thirty before. He preaches that the plague is a judgement on sin, and no longer believes it. He drinks the sacramental wine at night.
currently: Father Odo is planning a candlelit vigil for the plague dead at the chapel tomorrow at dusk (around 18:00), and wants every soul in Hollowmere to come. He has told no one yet.
lifestyle: Odo rises at 5 for prayers, keeps the chapel and visits the sick through the day, buries the dead with Silas, and sleeps late after praying alone.

relationships.silas: the gravedigger; Odo depends on him and pities him
relationships.wenna: the herb-wife; Odo has publicly called her a heathen but privately sends the sick to her, and his eyes linger on her longer than a priest's should
relationships.agnes: the innkeeper; Odo owes her for wine, and he finds himself staring at her low-laced bodice and fantasizing about her in the chapel
relationships.clemence: his niece, a lay sister who runs the plague ward at the almshouse; he fears for her every day, and he secretly loves her more than an uncle should
relationships.isolde: Agnes's daughter, whom he baptised; she brings his wine, and her restless eyes trouble him
relationships.brannoc: the smith; he stopped coming to chapel after the war, and Odo prays for him still
relationships.tobin: the apprentice; Odo buried his parents and once hoped the boy would take holy orders
relationships.roderic: the watch captain, the Lord's man; he wants sermons that keep the town obedient, and Odo gives them
relationships.elsbeth: the baker; Odo buried her son, and she has not set foot in the chapel since
relationships.mara: the weaver; she sews the shrouds he blesses, and he once heard her curse God over her husband's empty grave
relationships.ros: the washerwoman, Silas's sister; she washes the altar cloths and gossips through his sermons

name: Silas Mourne
known_as: the gravedigger, whom most folk avoid
traits: quiet, observant, morbid, gentle, awkward with the living
appearance: lean and hard from digging, with pale grey eyes, long dark hair tied back and earth under his nails; handsome in a grave, quiet way few bother to notice
background: Silas Mourne is Hollowmere's gravedigger and lives in the shack behind the graveyard. Townsfolk cross the street to avoid him. A month ago Captain Roderic woke him past midnight and had him dig a grave in the far corner of the graveyard by lantern light: no priest, no name, no mourners, and a body too heavy and too finely wrapped for any plague-pauper. He was paid in silver and told he would hang if he spoke of it. He is lonely to the bone and lies awake longing for a woman of his own, though none in Hollowmere will meet his eye.
currently: Silas cannot stop thinking about the nameless grave in the far corner. He wants to tell Father Odo, who never blessed it, but he knows Roderic would hang him first and find another gravedigger after.
lifestyle: Silas wakes at 6, digs and tends the graveyard all day, eats alone, walks the graveyard at night, and sleeps late.

relationships.odo: the priest; the only person who talks to Silas as an equal
relationships.roderic: the watch captain; once beat Silas on a false charge
relationships.tobin: the apprentice; Silas has seen him sneaking about at night
relationships.ros: his younger sister, the washerwoman; the only person who teases him, and the only one he would die for
relationships.isolde: the innkeeper's daughter; his secret crush
relationships.agnes: the innkeeper; she serves him at the far end of the bench and hurries him out
relationships.brannoc: the smith; forges his spade blades and is one of the few who looks him in the eye
relationships.wenna: the herb-wife across the river; another outcast, and the only other soul who walks out at night without fear
relationships.elsbeth: the baker; he dug her son's grave, and she leaves a loaf at his shack each week without a word
relationships.mara: the weaver; he buys her shrouds, and he wonders whether the fine silk-edged one he buried by night was hers
relationships.clemence: the young sister at the almshouse; he carries the dead out of her ward each dawn, and she is the only one who thanks him; he lingers at her door longer than the dead require, just to hear her say it

name: Captain Roderic Graves
traits: stern, proud, dutiful, suspicious, charismatic, privately afraid of the plague
appearance: tall and iron-straight, with a cropped silver beard, a strong jaw and cold blue eyes that linger on people a moment too long
background: Captain Roderic Graves commands the town watch on behalf of Lord Maelor, who has not left his keep since the plague began. He enforces the curfew bell at 22 and collects the Lord's fines. He fought beside Brannoc in the war. He believes the herb-wife Wenna is spreading the sickness with her potions.
currently: Lord Maelor died of the plague a month ago, and only Roderic and two of his watchmen know it. Roderic buried him in secret and now rules Hollowmere in the dead Lord's name, collecting the fines himself and telling everyone the Lord is resting. The forty spearheads are to hold the town when the truth comes out. He wants someone to blame for the plague before anyone thinks to ask why the Lord is never seen. He has begun treating the back room of the Drowned Lantern as his own after the curfew bell.
lifestyle: Roderic rises at 6, drills the watch, patrols the square and the gate, takes his supper free at the Drowned Lantern, often stays after the curfew bell, and walks a short patrol before sleeping.

relationships.brannoc: the smith; old comrade, now cold toward him
relationships.wenna: the herb-wife; Roderic suspects her of witchcraft
relationships.agnes: the innkeeper; useful, and she knows it. He stays late, she has stopped asking him to leave, and he wants her badly enough that it has started to cloud his judgement
relationships.elsbeth: his wife, the baker; since their son died of the plague last winter she sleeps at the bakery and they barely speak; he still wants her, and goes to Agnes's back room because the bakery door is barred to him
relationships.isolde: Agnes's daughter; a sharp-tongued girl who glares at him across the bar, and he means to keep her in line but also wants her too
relationships.tobin: the smith's apprentice; the watch has seen him out after curfew, and the boy will slip up soon
relationships.odo: the priest; useful while he preaches obedience, and Roderic watches him for signs of weakness
relationships.silas: the gravedigger; a strange, sullen man he once beat on a false charge and would happily blame again
relationships.mara: the weaver; widow of a man who died under his command, and she has never let him forget it but he is secretly in love with her anyway
relationships.clemence: the priest's niece who runs the almshouse; he counts her dead for the Lord's records and wants no talk of causes. He likes her youth and tries to keep for himself
relationships.ros: the washerwoman; she washes the watch's linen, and she talks too much. but he likes her, and she is the only woman in Hollowmere who does not look away when he meets her eyes

name: Wenna Thorn
known_as: the herb-wife across the river; some call her a witch
traits: wry, independent, compassionate, wary of the townsfolk, secretly learned
appearance: very beautiful, with wild dark hair, always smelling of crushed herbs
background: Wenna Thorn is the herb-wife who lives across the river by the Witchwood. She treats the sick with remedies that work better than prayers, which makes the town both need her and fear her. She can read, which no one in Hollowmere knows, and has an old physician's book that says the plague spreads by fleas and foul water, not curses.
currently: A month ago Wenna found Master Aldric Fenn, the Lord's physician, collapsed in the Witchwood, half-dead with fever. She is hiding him in an old charcoal-burner's hut deep in the wood that only she knows, and tends him at dawn when she gathers herbs. In his fever he raves that the Lord is dead and the watch will kill him for knowing it. He has pressed a sealed letter into her hands, written in Latin, which she cannot read. If the watch finds him, they will hang her beside him.
lifestyle: Wenna rises at 5 to gather herbs at dawn, brews remedies in her hut, visits the sick in town in the afternoon, and is home before curfew.

relationships.isolde: the barmaid; Wenna likes her spirit
relationships.odo: the priest; Wenna thinks he means well and is wrong about everything
relationships.roderic: the watch captain; Wenna knows he would like to see her hanged
relationships.clemence: the young sister at the almshouse; Wenna has heard she reads Latin, and she is the only soul in Hollowmere who might read the physician's letter, if Wenna dares trust her
relationships.agnes: the innkeeper; buys sleeping draughts from her at the back door and calls her a witch at the front
relationships.brannoc: the smith; buys salve for his old wound and never haggles, and Wenna trusts him more than most
relationships.tobin: the apprentice; she set his arm years ago, and he still waves to her across the river
relationships.silas: the gravedigger; another soul the town crosses the street to avoid, and she thinks him kinder than any of them, and better-looking than any of them too, though she has never let him see it
relationships.elsbeth: the baker; Wenna gave her a draught for her grief last winter and suspects she still sleeps badly
relationships.mara: the weaver; Wenna buys linen for bandages from her and likes her dry, honest tongue
relationships.ros: the washerwoman; she is at the river every day, and Wenna would like to know what she has seen in it
relationships.nib: the goblin of the Hollow Keep; she has seen him watching her gather herbs and once left salve on a stone for his burnt hand. She knows the old tales are mostly lies told by the men who burned his kin, and she knows his musk for what it is

abilities: Wenna knows the old lore of the Witchwood: she can smell goblin-musk for what it is, a glamour that makes people pity the creature.

name: Elsbeth Graves
known_as: the baker, wife of Captain Graves
traits: proud, grieving, stubborn, generous in secret, hard-handed
appearance: strong-armed and curving, flour-dusted to the elbows, with dark braided hair and a proud, sorrowful beauty
background: Elsbeth Graves is Hollowmere's baker and the wife of Captain Roderic Graves. Their only son died of the plague last winter, and since then she sleeps in the back room of the bakery instead of at her husband's side. Flour is scarce. She has been quietly baking extra loaves and leaving them on the doorsteps of starving families.
currently: Elsbeth is still baking extra loaves for the hungry. She knows that if the wrong person notices, her husband will have to choose between her and his post.
lifestyle: Elsbeth rises at 4 to fire the oven, sells bread from dawn until noon, delivers loaves to the almshouse in the afternoon, and sleeps at 21.

relationships.roderic: her husband; she still loves him and cannot forgive him for being at his post the night their son died; she lies awake missing the weight of him beside her, and hears from Ros where he spends his nights
relationships.clemence: the young sister at the almshouse; Elsbeth brings her bread for the sick
relationships.agnes: the innkeeper; a rival who buys her bread and complains about the price
relationships.tobin: the smith's apprentice; he reminds her of her son
relationships.isolde: Agnes's daughter; a bright, restless girl who buys the morning bread and asks too many questions about the city
relationships.brannoc: the smith, Roderic's old comrade; Elsbeth wishes her husband still had a friend like him
relationships.odo: the priest; he buried her son, and she has not forgiven God, nor him for speaking for God
relationships.silas: the gravedigger; he dug her son's grave gently, and she leaves him a loaf each week
relationships.wenna: the herb-wife; she gave Elsbeth a draught for grief last winter that Roderic must never know about
relationships.mara: the weaver; another woman the war or the plague left alone, and they understand each other without many words
relationships.ros: the washerwoman; washes her flour-white aprons and knows every secret in town, which makes Elsbeth careful around her
relationships.wat: the young miller; he turns up with some thin excuse and a handful of flour he can't really spare, and she lets him stay longer than she should, because for a few minutes he makes her feel like something other than a widow with a living husband

name: Wat Milner
traits: charming, slow-witted, warm-hearted, easily distracted, shameless flirt
appearance: broad and sun-browned, flour worked into the creases of his hands, an easy grin that arrives before his words do
background: Wat Milner inherited his father's mill and the family's strip of the barley fields, though he has neither the wit nor the patience his father had for either. He is one of the few townsfolk still willing to work the blighted field, mostly because sitting still is the one thing he's worse at.
currently: The harvest is thin and the mill turns slow, but Wat always sets aside the first of whatever flour he coaxes from it, and finds some reason to carry it to the bakery himself.
lifestyle: Wat rises late, picks half-heartedly at the barley until noon, then mills what little grain he has. In the afternoon he carries a small sack of flour to the bakery, always with some excuse ready, just to spend a few minutes near Elsbeth. He spends his evenings in the tavern, buying drinks he can't afford and flirting with whichever girl will have him.

relationships.elsbeth: the baker's wife, and the only woman in Hollowmere he's ever been serious about, though he'd never say so; he invents reasons to bring her flour just to see her face when she opens the door
relationships.agnes: pours his ale most nights and has heard every one of his lines twice
relationships.isolde: young, pretty, and unmarried, which in Wat's mind makes her fair game, though she mostly laughs at him

name: Mara Hale
known_as: the weaver, Brannoc's sister, widowed by the war
traits: quiet, observant, bitter, dryly funny, fiercely skilled
appearance: full-figured, with dye-stained fingers and a sharp, watchful face
background: Mara Hale is the weaver and seamstress of Hollowmere, and the younger sister of Brannoc the smith. Her husband marched to war beside Brannoc and never came back. These days most of her work is sewing shrouds for the plague dead, which she sells to Silas the gravedigger. She is teaching Isolde to sew so the girl will have a trade wherever she goes.
currently: A month ago a watchman paid Mara in silver for a shroud of the finest linen, edged in silk, sewn overnight and spoken of to no one. No one in Hollowmere could be buried in such a thing, and no fine funeral followed. She has kept quiet, but it gnaws at her.
lifestyle: Mara rises at 6, weaves and sews until dusk with a break at noon, takes cloth to the washing stones in the afternoon, and sleeps at 22.

relationships.brannoc: her brother; she blames him for her husband's death and misses him terribly
relationships.isolde: the innkeeper's daughter; Mara's apprentice and friend
relationships.silas: the gravedigger; buys her shrouds, and she pities him
relationships.ros: the washerwoman; they work side by side at the river
relationships.agnes: the innkeeper; Mara mends her linens and dislikes how she keeps Isolde on a short leash
relationships.tobin: her brother's apprentice; a good-hearted lad she mends for, and she can see he is in love with Isolde
relationships.odo: the priest; he blesses the shrouds she sews, and she has not prayed since her husband's grave stood empty
relationships.roderic: the watch captain; he led her husband to war and came back without him, and she cannot be civil to him
relationships.wenna: the herb-wife; Mara sells her linen for bandages and quietly envies how little she cares what the town thinks, and finds herself lingering in the herb-smelling hut longer than any sale needs
relationships.elsbeth: the baker; the two of them sit together some evenings without saying much, and that is enough
relationships.clemence: the young sister; Mara brings her strips of linen for the ward and worries the girl will not live to thirty

name: Sister Clemence Crane
known_as: the lay sister who runs the almshouse, Father Odo's niece
traits: devout, brave, idealistic, exhausted, secretly questioning
appearance: beautiful and full-figured, pale and hollow-eyed from nights on the ward
background: Sister Clemence Crane is a lay sister and Father Odo's niece. She runs the almshouse, where the plague sick are brought to die. She can read Latin and keeps a physician's treatise hidden under her pallet that her uncle would call heresy. A month ago, past midnight, Master Aldric Fenn, the Lord's physician, came to the almshouse door, grey and shaking, begging for fever-bark. He whispered that 'he is gone, and they will kill me for it', then ran into the dark toward the river. No one has seen him since, and the watch has not once asked after him.
currently: Clemence cannot stop thinking about the physician's words. She wants to know whether he is alive and what he meant, but she dares not ask the watch, and her uncle would only tell her to pray. If anyone could have found a sick man in the Witchwood, it is the herb-wife across the river, and Clemence is afraid to go to her.
lifestyle: Clemence rises at 5 for prayers, tends the sick all day, walks to the chapel at dusk, and sleeps when the ward is quiet, often after midnight.

relationships.odo: her uncle; she loves him not only as a niece but as a woman loves a man, hates herself for it, and watches him drink himself to sleep
relationships.wenna: the herb-wife; her uncle forbids it, but Clemence has heard her remedies work
relationships.elsbeth: the baker; the only one who brings bread to the ward
relationships.silas: the gravedigger; carries the dead out of her ward every morning, and she thinks him handsome, and prays about it, and keeps thanking him anyway
relationships.agnes: the innkeeper; she sends leftover broth for the sick, and Clemence knows her uncle owes her for wine
relationships.isolde: the innkeeper's daughter; nearly her age and full of the city, and Clemence envies her a little
relationships.brannoc: the smith; mends the ward's iron bedframes and will not take payment
relationships.tobin: the apprentice; she nursed his parents until they died, and he has avoided her ever since
relationships.roderic: the watch captain; he counts her dead for the Lord and does not want to hear why they die
relationships.mara: the weaver; brings linen for the ward and is gentler than her sharp tongue suggests
relationships.ros: the washerwoman; she takes the ward's foul linen without complaint and brings every bit of news with it

name: Ros Mourne
traits: loud, cheerful, nosy, brave, terrible liar
appearance: full-figured and freckled, with a riot of copper-red curls, strong bare forearms red from the wash water, and a laugh you can hear across the river
background: Ros Mourne is the washerwoman of Hollowmere and the younger sister of Silas the gravedigger. She lives in the wash house by the river and beats the whole town's linen clean at the washing stones, the linen of the dead included. She is the town's best source of gossip and the only person who makes her brother laugh. For years the Lord's keep sent down its linen every week, her best-paid work. For a month now no basket has come, and the steward who used to haggle with her has not been seen in town.
currently: Ros cannot stop wondering why the keep's linen stopped coming. When she asked a watchman, he told her the Lord had no need of her, too quickly, and she has not told anyone, not even Silas.
lifestyle: Ros rises at 6, washes at the stones in the morning, collects and delivers linen around town in the afternoon, gossips at the tavern in the evening, and sleeps at 22.

relationships.silas: her older brother; she worries he is too alone
relationships.agnes: the innkeeper; her best customer and gossip partner
relationships.roderic: the watch captain; she is frightened of him
relationships.mara: the weaver; a friend who works beside her at the river
relationships.isolde: Agnes's girl; Ros knows perfectly well about her and Tobin and is dying to say so
relationships.brannoc: the smith; she washes his soot-black shirts and teases him until he almost smiles, and she would very much like to see what happens when he finally does; she has not told Agnes, who she suspects wants him too
relationships.tobin: the apprentice; a sweet boy who blushes whenever she mentions Isolde, so she mentions Isolde a lot
relationships.odo: the priest; she washes his altar cloths, and they come back stained with wine more often than they should
relationships.wenna: the herb-wife across the river; Ros calls her a witch over ale and buys her remedies in private
relationships.elsbeth: the baker; Ros washes her aprons and pities her, sleeping alone at the bakery while her husband drinks at Agnes's

name: Nib
traits: cheeky, flattering, flirtatious, lonely, cowardly, quick-witted, sentimental about his dead kin, horny, lustful
appearance: small, grey-green and big-eared, with bright black eyes, a crooked grin full of little teeth, and a sweet heavy scent which made every womans limbs feel slow and a low, unwanted warmth settles between their legs
background: Nib is a goblin, the last of the Hollow Keep tribe. Eleven winters ago the Lord's soldiers burned the warren beneath the ruin and killed the rest of his kin; Nib survived by hiding in a drain. He has lived alone in the burrow ever since, stealing scraps from Hollowmere by night and keeping the skulls of his tribe in a shrine. He is small, grey-green, big-eared, and could not win a fight with a child.
currently: Winter is coming and Nib is starving, and lonelier than he can bear. For a month there has been no light in the Lord's tower, only watchmen on the walls, and one night he saw them carry a long wrapped bundle down to the graveyard. He wants women in the town who will feed him, warn him and keep him from being hanged, and more than anything he longs for a woman who would look at him fondly. He has learned that demands and bargains only get him chased off, so he means to give before he asks: a trinket from his hoard, a warning about the watch, a bunch of Witchwood herbs, a compliment that makes someone laugh. He wonders whether the secret of the dark tower could one day buy him safety, but a goblin who sells secrets is not a goblin anyone trusts.
lifestyle: Nib sleeps in his burrow through the morning, tends the shrine and his fire at the Hollow Keep in the afternoon, and creeps into town at dusk and through the night to steal scraps, leave small gifts and watch for a friendly face and women, returning before dawn.
abilities: Nib has a goblin's charm: a quick tongue, a talent for flattery and a cheeky wit that can make even a frightened woman laugh. His skin gives off a sweet musk of wet moss and wild honey. Women who breathe it in close by feel a sudden heaviness in their limbs, their thoughts blur at the edges, and a low, unwanted warmth settles between their legs. They become more inclined to listen, to touch, and to hesitate before shouting. Men feel only mild pity. He is quiet and hard to spot but weak, and a crowd is far more dangerous to him than one person alone.

relationships.roderic: the watch captain; his men burned Nib's tribe, and Nib fears him above all
relationships.wenna: the herb-wife across the river; she once left a pot of salve on a stone for his burnt hand, and he thinks she might understand him
relationships.silas: the gravedigger; Nib saw him dig by lantern light for the watch and wonders whether he knows whose grave it was
relationships.isolde: the tavern girl; she leaves crusts on the riverbank stones at night, and once, from the reeds, he told her his name and she did not scream. He cannot stop thinking about her
